draft.why_angle: The cited RTINGS lists and The Hook Up's 2026 portable guide give no battery-mode brightness for the MoGo 4, Capsule 3 or Vibe One. None of them says the advertised battery hours only hold in a dimmer Eco mode. This page puts each maker's Eco-only runtime rating next to the lumens a named lab measured in that mode, and adds the power-bank wattage each model accepts.

page.title: Best Mini Projector Under $500 (2026): Battery Hours vs Real Brightness
page.h1: Best mini projector under $500: how bright each one is on battery
page.desc: Five portable 1080p mini projectors under $500. The battery hours they advertise are Eco-mode hours, so this compares the brightness labs measured in that mode, and which power banks run each one.
page.answer: Short answer. The best portable mini projector under $500 is the XGIMI MoGo 4. Its 2.5-hour battery rating applies to Eco mode, where ProjectorCentral measured 154 lumens of brightness. In its review, the cheaper Vibe One gave 64 lumens on battery.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Light on battery, MoGo 4 vs Vibe One: 154 ÷ 64 = 2.4 times the light at each one's rated battery setting.
  • MoGo 4 vs Capsule 3 on battery: 154 ÷ 112 = 1.4 times. Their spec sheets (450 ISO vs 200 ANSI) suggest 2.25 times.
  • Brightness kept in Eco: MoGo 4 154 ÷ 404 = 38%; Vibe One 64 ÷ 229 = 28%; Capsule 3 112 ÷ 161 = 70% (both Capsule figures from The Hook Up).
  • Two-hour films per charge at the maker's rating: MoGo 4 2.5 ÷ 2 = 1.25; Capsule 3 2.5 ÷ 2 = 1.25 (The Hook Up's 2 h 53 min run gives 1.4); Vibe One 1.2 ÷ 2 = 0.6.
  • Cost per rated lumen when plugged in: Elfin Flip Plus 399 ÷ 500 = 0.80 dollars; MoGo 2 Pro (New) 359 ÷ 430 = 0.83 dollars; Vibe One 249 ÷ 250 = 1.00 dollar.
UseFits
Backyard or campsite movie with no outletXGIMI MoGo 4 {buy:xgimi-mogo-4}
Smallest battery projector for a dark tent or bedroom, with a 45 W bank you already ownNebula Capsule 3 (Google TV)
Brightest picture for the money, always plugged inXGIMI Elfin Flip Plus
Plug-in projector with dual 8 W Dolby Audio speakersXGIMI MoGo 2 Pro (New)
Lowest price, used plugged in by the bed or on the ceilingXGIMI Vibe One

Battery hours are Eco-mode hours

XGIMI's MoGo 4 page says it plainly: "In Eco Mode, the built-in battery provides up to 2.5 hours of video playback." The same page says the 450 ISO lumen rating was measured in Performance (High Power) mode, so the brightness figure and the battery figure come from different settings. ProjectorCentral measured the MoGo 4 at 400–404 lumens in Performance, 258–270 in Standard and 151–154 in Eco. Its Standard-mode battery lasted through a 90-minute film. Expert Reviews measured 1 h 52 min of streaming in Standard. So a full film at the brighter setting fits on one charge, but only just.

Nebula's Capsule 3 spec line reads "Battery Life (Eco Mode) 2.5 Hrs". The Hook Up measured 161 lumens plugged in and 112 on battery in Eco. ProjectorCentral found that the Vibe One drops into Eco on its own when unplugged (you can turn that off) and measured 58–64 lumens there, against 229 plugged in. XGIMI rates it for 1.2 hours of video.

Power banks extend some of these but not others. The MoGo 4 takes USB-C PD at 65–150 W (XGIMI), so a 45 W bank falls short. UGREEN's 145W 25,000 mAh bank (90 Wh, 140 W from its first USB-C port) falls inside that range {buy:ugreen-145w-25000mah-3-port-power-bank}. Nebula lets the Capsule 3 charge from a bank of 45 W or more at 5–20 V. The Vibe One has a DC barrel input and no USB-C charging, according to Android Authority. The Elfin Flip Plus also uses a DC jack: The Hook Up ran it for 90 minutes from a 20,000 mAh bank through a 20 V USB-C-to-barrel converter.

Not recommended

XGIMI Vibe One as a battery projector. Its 1.2-hour rating is shorter than most films. Android Authority got 96 minutes "on a good run", and ProjectorCentral measured 64 lumens on battery and called the runtime "too short for most feature-length films". Plugged in it measures 229 lumens, which makes it a reasonable low-cost bedroom projector, but not a portable one.

log: Confirmed (read 2026-11-14): MoGo 4 page shows 71.28 Wh, 'Up to 2.5 Hours Video Playtime (Eco Mode)', 450 ISO tested in Performance/High Power mode, and power-bank output 65–150 W. The page shows no price.

Confirmed: ProjectorCentral MoGo 4 measured Performance 400–404, Standard 258–270 and Eco 151–154 (Movie mode Eco = 154). In Standard power mode the battery lasted through the 90-minute War of the Worlds. Rated 450 ISO.
Confirmed: Expert Reviews measured 1 hr 52 mins streaming in Standard mode and says Eco gives 'a noticeable dip in brightness'.

Confirmed: ProjectorCentral Vibe One measured 196–229 (Performance), 172–194 (Standard) and 58–64 (Eco/battery); auto-Eco on battery 'can be turned off'; rated 250 ISO and 1.2 h in ECO; Cons line reads 'Battery life is too short for most feature-length films'.
Confirmed: Android Authority says 'No USB-C charging', DC charger, and 'only lasts 96 minutes on a good run'.
Confirmed: soundcore Capsule 3 page says 200 ANSI lumens, Battery Life (Eco Mode) 2.5 Hrs, PD 20V/2.25A. The soundcore service article gives ≥45 W, PD2.0, 5–20 V for Capsule 3.

Confirmed: The Hook Up Capsule 3 review gives 161 lm plugged in, 112 lm in battery Eco, and 2 h 53 min runtime. The Hook Up 2026 guide gives Elfin Flip Plus 484 lm (High-Performance) and 345 lm (Standard), 90 min on a 20,000 mAh UGREEN bank via a 20 V USB-C-to-barrel converter, and does not cover MoGo 4, Capsule 3 or Vibe One (consistent with why_angle).
